A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 33-page versions of the same GeoRCG paper. Full-document comparison establishes identical extracted text and rendered pages on pages 2–33, including Appendices A–E; differences are confined to page 1.

before.justification: v3 reports original GeoRCG experiments on QM9 and GEOM-DRUG, including unconditional and conditional generation results in Section 4 and additional experiments in Appendices A and C.

after.justification: v4 retains the original GeoRCG generation experiments, numerical results, ablations and generated-sample visualizations in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain the same two-stage GeoRCG procedure, EDM/SemlaFlow variants, training objectives, representation perturbation and sampling guidance.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same encoder pretraining data, unconditional generation coverage on QM9 and GEOM-DRUG, and six-property conditional generation coverage on QM9.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in corresponding experiments, including EDM, GeoLDM and GeoBFN in Table 1, SemlaFlow/MiDi/EQGAT-diff in Table 2, and LDM-3DG in Tables 3 and 8.

E3.justification: The QM9 half-split for conditional evaluation, 10,000-sample evaluations, metrics, sampling-step sweeps and training settings in Section 4 and Appendices A–B are unchanged.

E4.justification: The quality/diversity sweeps, encoder and perturbation/dropout ablations, conditional-molecule quality checks and Appendix E visual analyses are identical, including Figures 4 and 6 and Tables 10–12.

E5.justification: Section 4.1 specifies the same three-run averaging and standard errors reported in parentheses. Neither run information nor uncertainty-reporting practices change.

E6.justification: All numerical tables and result figures are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports GeoRCG (EDM) QM9 molecule stability of 92.32% and validity of 96.52% in both versions.

T1.justification: Proposition 3.1, Theorem 3.2 and the assumptions, bounds and proofs in Appendix D are identical. The mathematical derivations elsewhere are also unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same GeoRCG contributions and claims about generation quality, approximately 50% conditional-generation improvement and substantially fewer diffusion steps.

C2.justification: Interpretations of representation guidance and the quality/diversity tradeoff are unchanged. Section 5 retains the same limitations concerning encoder quality and classifier-free-guidance resource overhead.

D1.justification: v4 adds a code-availability sentence and GeoRCG GitHub repository link to the abstract; v3 contains no corresponding repository link. Implementation, hyperparameter and hardware disclosures otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 removes the EDM and SemlaFlow citation parentheticals from the abstract, but both works remain cited and discussed elsewhere. The cited-work set, related-work discussion and research positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract loses two citation parentheticals and gains a code-availability sentence, while the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. The remaining prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Visual edits are confined to abstract reflow, the added hyperlink and the updated first-page arXiv stamp. All figures, tables and layouts on pages 2–33 are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new repository link gives readers an explicit route to the implementation that v3 lacked, modestly improving reproducibility information. The scientific evidence and reasoning remain unchanged, and the works whose abstract citations were removed remain cited elsewhere.
